perf.summary: Hoist the four per-iteration stackalloc buffers (parent, parentEdge, dist, inqueue) out of the while(true) augmentation loop.
perf.currentCost: Lines 14-17 allocate 4 stack buffers (parent: n*4B, parentEdge: n*4B, dist: n*8B, inqueue: n*1B = ~17n bytes) on every single augmenting-path iteration. There can be O(V*E) augmentations; the stack pointer churns each loop and the buffers are re-zeroed/re-filled anyway at line 18 (and dist again inside Spfa at line 33).
perf.proposedChange: Move the four `stackalloc` declarations above `while (true)` (line 12). Keep the per-iteration reset loop at line 18 as-is (it already reinitializes all of dist/parent/inqueue each pass). Spfa's cnt and q buffers can likewise be allocated once and passed in, or Spfa's internal dist re-init (line 33) can be dropped since Run already sets dist on line 18 immediately before the call.
perf.rationale: stackalloc in a loop does not free per iteration in C#; the frame grows only once, but emitting the localloc/zeroing pattern each iteration adds instructions and defeats the JIT/Burst hoisting it could do if declared once. One allocation + a tight reset loop is strictly fewer instructions and a smaller, stable working set that stays hot in L1.
perf.risk: None for buffer hoisting: every element is unconditionally rewritten by the line-18 reset loop before use. If also removing the duplicate dist init at line 33, confirm Spfa is only ever called right after the line-18 reset (it is) — otherwise keep it. Stack frame size is unchanged or smaller.

perf.summary: Eliminate the duplicate dist[] initialization performed in both Run (line 18) and Spfa (line 33).
perf.currentCost: dist[i] = long.MaxValue is written for all i at line 18, then immediately overwritten with the identical value for all i at line 33 inside Spfa. That is a redundant O(n) pass over an 8n-byte buffer every augmentation, plus a second streaming write that evicts nothing useful.
perf.proposedChange: Remove the loop `for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) dist[i] = long.MaxValue;` at line 33 in Spfa (Run already initialized dist on line 18). Alternatively remove the dist part of line 18 and keep line 33. Keep exactly one.
perf.rationale: Halves the dist-initialization memory traffic per augmentation (one 8n-byte streaming write instead of two). On mobile with limited bandwidth this is a measurable constant-factor win in the hot augmentation loop.
perf.risk: Must guarantee Spfa is always invoked immediately after the line-18 reset with no intervening dist mutation. In this file Spfa is called only on line 19 right after line 18, so safe. dist[s]=0 is set in Spfa (line 34) after, so ordering is preserved.
